additions.site_name: AtlasEdge DUS001 Düsseldorf Data Centre (Zum Jägerhof 10, Hilden)
additions.name: AtlasEdge DUS001 Düsseldorf — operating data centre

status.summary: AtlasEdge's Düsseldorf page, in its version modified on 14 August 2026, lists DUS001 at Zum Jägerhof 10, 40724 Hilden as 'In operation' and names the carriers 'currently operational at this site'. The Internet Archive copies of 28 June and 2 August 2026 (the preceding version, dated 13 November 2025) carry the same label, so the label was re-published in a version made after 2 August. Operation of the DUS001 facility is established as of 14 August 2026, the version's modification day. The current version's capacity figures (6,160 m2 white space, 11.2 MW IT) repeat the operator's Stuttgart page word for word, and the preceding version gave 10,000 m2 and 20 MW, so no capacity in service is asserted.

locator.precision: Centroid of cadastral parcel Gemarkung Hilden, Flur 25, Flurstück 271, the only parcel with location text 'Zum Jägerhof 10' (14,225 m2 of industrial and commercial land, about 198 by 156 m). The point marks the DUS001 property. The official June 2025 orthophoto shows the data-centre building in the parcel's north-western part and the point in the yard just east of it, so the point is not a building footprint centroid, an entrance or a works extent.
locator.identity_review: AtlasEdge gives DUS001's address as Zum Jägerhof 10, 40724 Hilden, in the current page and in the archived versions of 28 June and 2 August 2026. NRW ALKIS returns 21 Hilden parcels with 'Jägerhof' in their location text; only Flurstück 271 is 'Zum Jägerhof 10', and its actual use is industrial and commercial land. The ALKIS building layer records no building on the parcel, but the official orthophoto of 20 June 2025 shows a large flat-roofed building with rows of rooftop and side-mounted plant units on it, consistent with an operating data centre whose footprint is not yet in the cadastral building layer. Zum Jägerhof 2 and the unnumbered street and woodland parcels are excluded.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The ALKIS service publishes no positional accuracy. The centroid represents a 14,225 m2 parcel (105 m to its farthest vertex); the building's own footprint is not in the cadastral building layer, and its offset from the point (visually within about 20 m of its eastern wall) is not surveyed.

status.summary: noris network's Rechenzentrum München page, in its version modified on 19 August 2026, presents the Rechenzentrum München Ost in Aschheim (MUC5), opened in mid-2017 and expanded in 2019, in the present tense as its operating colocation data centre: it offers high-density racks, on-site 24/7 support, DE-CIX services and KyotoCooling, with 11,000 m2 total and 8,700 m2 IT area. The Internet Archive holds the same version on 12 October 2026, and the operator's locations page (version of 7 September 2026, bounded by archive copies of 7 May and 5 October) lists the München Ost data centre at Klausnerstraße 30, 85609 Aschheim. Operation is established as of 19 August 2026; the 2017 opening and 2019 expansion are history, not the observation. The areas are operator facility figures, not a measured load.

locator.precision: Footprint centroid of the official LoD2 building addressed 'Klausnerstraße 30', Aschheim (DEBY_LOD2_105260186; 481.8 m2, about 36 by 31 m, 16.2 m high), the street-side entrance and office block of the data-centre complex. Two connected buildings without address (11,800 m2 combined footprint) adjoin it within the same parcel to the south-east and appear to hold the data halls; their combined centroid is 120.5 m from the point. The point therefore marks the site at its address, not the data-hall footprint.
locator.identity_review: noris network gives the München Ost data centre's address as Klausnerstraße 30, 85609 Aschheim on its locations page (versions of 7 May, 7 September and 5 October 2026). Exactly one building in the Bavarian LoD2 tiles 702_5336 and 702_5338 carries that address, in municipality 09184112 (Aschheim). The official parcel map shows house number 30 on this building, with two large connected buildings linked to it inside the same parcel strip; the August 2024 orthophoto shows rooftop plant housings on those buildings, and their 11,800 m2 combined footprint is consistent with the operator's 11,000 m2 total area. Klausnerstraße 34, a logistics building on a separate parcel 71 m east, and the locations page's street-centred map embed are excluded.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The LoD2 model publishes no numeric positional accuracy. The point is the centroid of a 482 m2 address building (18.5 m to its farthest vertex); the data-centre complex extends about 200 m south-east of it, and the halls' combined centroid lies 120.5 m away.

additions.site_name: Google New Albany Data Center Campus (1101 Beech Rd SW and 5266 Babbitt Rd)
additions.name: Google New Albany — existing data-centre campus operations

status.summary: The City of New Albany's data-center site, in its version modified on 26 August 2026, says the City 'is working to address noise complaints from neighbors near two active data center sites, one operated by Google and one operated by Meta', and that residents near 'Google's New Albany campus' reported noise from cooling fans, which Google is mitigating through sound monitoring, operational adjustments and sound-dampening materials, with a permanent solution scheduled for December 2026. This government statement records Google's New Albany campus as an active, Google-operated data-centre site on 26 August 2026, the modification day of the captured version (bounded by the Internet Archive copy of 6 September 2026 and the version's own reference to July 2026). It is not an opening, inspection or commissioning date; capacity, the number of buildings in service and occupancy are not established.

locator.precision: Planar centroid (computed in UTM 17N) of the union of Licking County Auditor parcel 094-106896-00.000 (1101 Beech Rd SW, 219.06 geodesic acres) and Franklin County tax parcel 222-004984 (5266 Babbitt Rd, 221.89 geodesic acres), both owned by Montauk Innovations LLC. The two parcels run along the Franklin-Licking county line for about 1,016 m with a 0.69 m gap between the two counties' polygons; their union covers 440.95 geodesic acres, about 1,834 by 1,654 m. The point lies inside the Licking parcel about 27 m from the county line. It locates the two-county campus property, not a building footprint, an entrance or a surveyed boundary.
locator.identity_review: The City of New Albany names 'Google's New Albany campus' and an active data-center site operated by Google, and its construction project list (16 April 2026 version, archived 29 September 2026) lists 'Google 7', a new 170,594 sq ft data center at 1101 Beech Road. Licking parcel 094-106896-00.000 is the parcel with site address 1101 Beech Rd SW; it is owned by Montauk Innovations LLC with owner mailing address 1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy, Mountain View, CA (Google's headquarters), carries land use 305 and 290.3 million USD of improvements, 244.0 million USD of them abated. The adjoining Franklin parcel 222-004984 has the same owner, the class description 'data center' and 207.6 million USD of buildings, and lies in the Plain Township-New Albany taxing district. Google's Ohio page says construction of its New Albany data center facility began in 2019, after the 2018-2019 transfers of both parcels. Montauk Innovations LLC's third parcel, 2565 Harrison Rd, is 4.68 km away, not contiguous, and is excluded (it is this fragment's separate HJS site). No geocoder, map viewport, city centre or business-park centroid is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: Neither county publishes positional accuracy for its parcel polygons, and the two counties' polygons leave a 0.69 m gap along the shared county line; the centroid represents a 441-acre two-parcel campus about 1,834 by 1,654 m, and the positions of the individual data-centre buildings within it are not published.

additions.site_name: DataBank Orangeburg Campus (LGA3 and LGA4, 2000 Corporate Drive, Orangetown)
additions.name: DataBank Orangeburg LGA3 — existing data-centre operations

status.summary: DataBank's news item of 10 August 2026 says, in DataBank's own words, that 'The Orangeburg facility supports healthcare, banking, and other digital services, and is one of several data centers located in the town', that DataBank 'is seeking to expand the existing site', and that the expansion is undergoing a full environmental impact study before it can go to the Orangetown Planning Board. The Orangeburg facility is LGA3, the campus's only built data center (DataBank says LGA4 'will be our second facility'). This records LGA3 as operating on 10 August 2026, the item's publication day; it is not an opening date, and the 20 MW is DataBank's stated critical IT load, not load in service. The expansion is not part of this record.

locator.precision: Planar centroid (computed in UTM 18N) of Rockland County tax parcel 73.15-1-19 in the Town of Orangetown, as published in the NYS public tax-parcel layer (33.41 calculated acres, about 449 by 641 m), the only parcel at 2000 Corporate Dr. It locates DataBank's 34-acre Orangeburg campus property, which holds LGA3 and the planned LGA4, not the LGA3 building footprint or a surveyed boundary.
locator.identity_review: DataBank gives 2000 Corporate Dr., Orangeburg, NY for both LGA3 and LGA4 on a 34-acre campus, and its May 2024 dedication release places the data-center site at 2000 Corporate Drive with LGA3 as the first building. An address query of the NYS public tax-parcel layer returns exactly one Rockland County parcel at 2000 Corporate Dr: 73.15-1-19 in Orangetown, 33.93 roll acres, property class 712, built 2025, 288,780 sq ft gross floor area, owner 2000 Corporate Drive LLC. The acreage matches the stated campus and the 2025 building matches the LGA3 construction. The roll's ZIP 10965 differs from DataBank's 10962, but street number and street match exactly. The owner LLC's relation to DataBank is not stated, so it is recorded only as owner. No geocoder, map viewport or town centre is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The state layer incorporates county parcel geometry as received and publishes no positional accuracy; the centroid represents a 33-acre parcel about 449 by 641 m, and the position of LGA3 within it is not published.
